title: Decision framework for Optimize eval actions and cohort thresholds
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define an operational decision framework and concrete acceptance thresholds for Optimize evaluations so that model and runtime changes can be rolled out safely with automated, cohort-aware rollback gates.
background: We currently have many overlapping eval documents focused on sampling, sentinel signals, and AB thresholds, but teams lack a single actionable decisioning matrix that maps statistical regression signals to rollout actions across cohorts and traffic horizons. This ticket consolidates requirements and acceptance criteria for the Optimize product review board and the rollout automation engineers.
scope: Deliver a PRD that: (1) defines primary/secondary quality metrics for Optimize evals; (2) specifies cohort stratification and sampling plan for canaries and AB tests; (3) prescribes statistical tests, SNR thresholds, and minimum sample sizes; (4) enumerates rollback triggers and corresponding remediation actions and SLAs; (5) supplies a small example playbook for a model change rollout.
out_of_scope: Implementation of the rollout automation, instrumentation dashboards, and data-pipeline fixes required to collect additional telemetry. Those are separate eng tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A single PRD document exists in Confluence called 'Optimize: Eval Decision Framework' and is linked from this ticket
Primary metric(s) are named and justified (e.g., per-customer correctness proxy, latency-adjusted utility) with backstop safety metric(s) for hallucination and toxicity
Cohorts are defined (at minimum: high-frequency API, long-context users, embeddings-only, enterprise vs. self-serve) with sampling allocation for canary phases (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%)
Statistical tests specified: pre-registered primary test alpha=0.01 (safety), alpha=0.05 (quality); use bootstrap CIs and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple cohorts
Minimum sample sizes and SNR thresholds are defined per cohort (e.g., SNR >= 1.5 preferred; if SNR < 0.8 flag for manual review before automated decisions)
Clear rollback matrix mapping signal severity to action: immediate full rollback, pause ramp and notify, continue with mitigation flag, or proceed (no action), with SLAs for each
A/B criteria include minimum detectable effect (MDE) per cohort, runtime stopping rules, and a requirement that at least 80% of cohorts show non-inferior primary metric before 100% ramp
Playbook example (change of decoder quantization profile) fleshes out monitoring queries, expected baselines, and the exact gating checks used during a 4-step canary ramp
Stakeholder reviews recorded from Eng/Design/Privacy with actionable feedback addressed (comments closed)
success_metrics: Reduction in manual rollbacks due to missed regressions (target: 50% year-over-year)
Time-to-detect critical regressions improved to < 5 minutes from first anomalous sample (for safety signals)
Fewer false-positive automated rollbacks (target: false rollback rate < 1% of canary runs)
decisions: Primary safety alpha fixed at 0.01 (conservative) while quality alpha remains 0.05 to balance sensitivity vs. developer velocity
Use stratified sampling by customer_tier + request_type as primary cohort keys; additional ad-hoc cohorts may be registered for targeted rollouts
Adopt bootstrap-based CIs for metric estimates and add Wolfowitz-like sequential stopping as a guard for long-running AB tests
Signal composition: severity score = weighted sum of normalized metric deltas where weights are product-defined; default weights will be set in the PRD and adjustable by project owners
open_tasks: Draft full PRD and upload to Confluence (owner: PM)
Sync with Applied ML on per-cohort SNR estimates using historical Optimize traffic (owner: Research)
Engineering spike to validate telemetry and compute minimum sample sizes for long-context cohort (owner: Eng Infra)
Design: mock up an 'eval gate' status card to show in Console during canaries
Security/Privacy review of cohort identifiers (owner: Security)
Finalize playbook example and pre-register tests in the rollout automation repo
